# Resource S3 Service

Create, delete, or modify S3 server

## Related ONTAP commands

```commandline
* vserver object-store-server show
* vserver object-store-server create
* vserver object-store-server modify
* vserver object-store-server delete
```

## Supported Platforms

* On-prem ONTAP system 9.8 or higher
* Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "netapp-ontap_s3_service" "s3_server_config" {
  cx_profile_name = "hw-cluster"
  svm_name = "svm1"
  name = "svm1.example.com"
  enabled = false
  comment = "not enabled"
  certificate_name = "svm1_1888D5C7BA7A2302"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cx_profile_name` (String) Connection profile name
- `name` (String) Specifies the name of the S3 server.
- `svm_name` (String) The name of the SVM.

### Optional

- `certificate_name` (String) Specifies the certificate that will be used for creating HTTPS connections to the S3 server.
- `comment` (String) Additional information about the server being created or modified.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Specifies whether or not the S3 service should be enabled.
- `is_http_enabled` (Boolean) Specifies whether HTTP is enabled on the S3 server being created or modified.
				By default, HTTP is disabled on the S3 server.
- `is_https_enabled` (Boolean) Specifies whether HTTPS is enabled on the S3 server being created or modified.
				By default, HTTPS is enabled on the S3 server.
- `port` (Number) Specifies the HTTP listener port for the S3 server.
				By default, HTTP is enabled on port 80. Valid values range from 1 to 65535.
- `secure_port` (Number) Specifies the HTTPS listener port for the S3 server.
				By default, HTTPS is enabled on port 443. Valid values range from 1 to 65535.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The name of the SVM.

~> **NOTE:** Disable the S3 server before modifying following fields: `is_http_enabled`, `is_https_enabled`, `port`, `secure_port`.

## Import

This resource supports import, which allows you to import existing S3 server configuration into the state of this resource.
Import require a unique ID composed of svm name and connection profile, separated by a comma.

id = `svm_name`,`cx_profile_name`

### Terraform Import

For example

```shell
 terraform import netapp-ontap_s3_service.example svm1,hw-cluster
```

!> The terraform import CLI command can only import resources into the state. Importing via the CLI does not generate configuration. If you want to generate the accompanying configuration for imported resources, use the import block instead.

### Terraform Import Block

This requires Terraform 1.5 or higher, and will auto create the configuration for you

First create the block

```terraform
import {
  to = netapp-ontap_s3_service.s3_service_import
  id = "svm1,hw-cluster"
}
```

Next run, this will auto create the configuration for you

```shell
terraform plan -generate-config-out=generated.tf
```

This will generate a file called generated.tf, which will contain the configuration for the imported resource

```terraform
# __generated__ by Terraform
# Please review these resources and move them into your main configuration files.
# __generated__ by Terraform from "svm1,hw-cluster"
resource "netapp-ontap_s3_service" "s3_service_import" {
  cx_profile_name = "hw-cluster"
  svm_name = "svm1"
}
```
